title: Sri Lanka shock New Zealand in Women’s T20 World Cup thriller - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Women secured a thrilling five-wicket victory over New Zealand Women in Match 7 of the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, successfully chasing down a target of 151 with two balls to spare at the Rose Bowl in Southampton.

After winning the toss, New Zealand elected to bat first and posted a competitive total of 150 for 6 in their allotted 20 overs. Captain Amelia Kerr and experienced all-rounder Sophie Devine led the scoring with 45 runs apiece, helping the White Ferns recover from a steady start. Sri Lanka’s bowlers maintained pressure throughout the innings, with Kavisha Dilhari producing the standout performance by claiming two wickets for 35 runs.

In response, Sri Lanka made a confident start to their chase, led by captain Chamari Athapaththu, who scored a quick 27 off 19 deliveries. However, New Zealand fought back through timely wickets, creating a tense contest during the middle overs. Despite the setbacks, Sri Lanka remained on course thanks to a composed innings from Nilakshi de Silva.

De Silva anchored the chase with a match-winning 54 off 37 balls, combining aggression with smart shot selection to keep Sri Lanka within reach of the target. Her innings proved decisive as the Sri Lankan batters held their nerve in the closing stages of the match.

Sri Lanka eventually reached 153 for 5 in 19.4 overs, sealing their first victory of the tournament and earning two valuable points in Group 2. The win provides a significant boost to their campaign following an opening defeat to England.

For New Zealand, the result marks a second consecutive loss in the competition, placing added pressure on the team ahead of its remaining group-stage fixtures. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, will look to build on the momentum as the tournament progresses.

title: 25% of private bus fleet operated on kerosene; LPBOA Chairman - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Lanka Private Bus Owners Association Chairman Gemunu Wijerathne has revealed that around 25 percent of the country’s private bus fleet had been operating using kerosene, describing the situation as a “tragic” and “illegal” practice within the sector.

Speaking to the media, Wijerathne said that while the association has been consistently demanding diesel allocations from the government, some bus owners had resorted to using kerosene intended for vulnerable communities.

He stressed that operating passenger buses on kerosene amounts to a major environmental concern and an unacceptable deviation from proper fuel usage standards.

Wijerathne further said that daily private bus operations have declined by nearly 25 percent following the recent increase in diesel prices.

He said an annual bus fare revision is scheduled for July, based on 12 key economic indicators, but the association has requested an interim fare adjustment to sustain operations amid rising fuel costs.

“Although bus services in Colombo are still running, operations in rural areas have been severely affected. Long-distance services are now operating based on passenger availability, and nearly 50 percent of journeys have been suspended,” he added.

title: Over 40% of schools found with Dengue breeding sites - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Dengue inspections carried out across Sri Lanka have revealed a high prevalence of mosquito breeding sites within school premises, Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

Speaking at the weekly Cabinet media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa stated that around 41% of locations inspected within the school system were found to contain dengue mosquito breeding sites.

He said inspections also detected breeding sites in 28% of religious places and 26% of industrial premises, highlighting the widespread nature of the problem.

The Minister noted that the dengue situation has become particularly severe in 14 districts and warned that the number of cases continues to rise in several parts of the country.

According to Dr. Jayatissa, increased case numbers have been reported in the Western and Southern Provinces, as well as in the districts of Kandy and Matale in the Central Province, Badulla, Batticaloa, two districts in the North Western Province, and both districts in the Sabaragamuwa Province.

He stressed that the success of the ongoing dengue prevention programme depends on the active participation of all sectors of society and called for coordinated efforts to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and curb the spread of the disease.

title: Namal thanks Nalinda for court reminder - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa said he was grateful to Minister Nalinda Jayatissa for reminding him of his upcoming court date and humorously requested that the minister remind him again before the hearing scheduled for next month.

Speaking on the matter, Rajapaksa said he had already written about the court case in his book and would remember that Minister Jayatissa had reminded him of the hearing.

“I have written about my court date in my book. I will remember that Hon. Minister Nalinda Jayatissa reminded me of the court date,” he said.

Rajapaksa added that the next court date falls on the 7th of next month and joked that another reminder from the minister would be helpful, given his busy schedule.

“I request him, the court date is on the 7th of next month. It would be good if he would remind me before that. These days I am asked to attend many meetings and so on, so if I forget, I will have a lot of work,” he said.

He further said he appreciated the minister’s reminder and extended an invitation to all 159 Members of Parliament to attend the court proceedings.

“I also invite him, and all 159 people, to come to court on that day and pay attention to the examination of evidence, rather than reading things here and there. Then they themselves can know how their police behaved,” Rajapaksa said.

title: Rs. 14m Kendu leaves, beedi seized in Chilaw coast guard raid - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Based on intelligence received, a special operation conducted by the Sri Lanka Coast Guard in coordination with the Sri Lanka Navy led to the arrest of a suspect and the seizure of a lorry transporting a large stock of illicit goods in the Kammala Wella beach area in Chilaw yesterday (15).

During the operation, authorities recovered over 2,000 kg of kendu leaves and 41,000 beedi sticks being transported in the lorry. The estimated street value of the seized consignment is believed to exceed Rs. 14 million.

The suspect, along with the seized stock and the vehicle, was handed over to the Excise Department Office in Biyagama for further investigations and legal proceedings.

title: Namal can continue campaigning when not attending court: Nalinda - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Cabinet spokesman and Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said it is acceptable for opposition politician Namal Rajapaksa to engage in campaign-related activities while travelling around the country, as long as he attends court proceedings on scheduled dates.

Responding to a journalist’s question regarding Rajapaksa’s ongoing political activities, the Minister said court obligations must take priority when hearings are scheduled.

“It’s fine. On days when there are court cases, he should attend court. On the other days, he can go around like that,” Jayatissa said.

title: Former Atamasthanadhipathi gives blood sample for DNA testing - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Former Anuradhapura Atamasthanadhipathi Ven. Pallegama Hemarathana Thera has provided a blood sample to the Government Analyst for DNA testing in connection with an ongoing investigation into alleged sexual abuse of a minor girl.

The sample was taken on Tuesday (16) after the monk was produced before the Government Analyst by officers of the Nittambuwa Police, in line with a directive issued by the Anuradhapura Chief Magistrate on June 12.

The court had ordered the suspect to provide a blood sample on June 16 and instructed that the Government Analyst submit the DNA report to court upon completion of the examination.

The order was issued after Nittambuwa Police informed court that clothing allegedly buried and concealed by the complainant had earlier been sent for forensic examination on May 4 under a previous court order.

Police said DNA testing on the items had revealed the presence of DNA alleles and sought court approval to obtain a blood sample from the suspect monk for comparison.

title: Rs. 15Bn project launched to upgrade BIA Terminal 1 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has launched a Rs. 15 billion project to renovate Terminal 1 of the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake, using domestic funds, authorities said.

The project is aimed at easing passenger congestion at the country’s main international airport until the completion of the Japan-assisted Terminal 2 development.

Under the upgrade, Terminal 1 will see expanded departure areas, redesigned arrival facilities and modernised baggage handling systems to improve efficiency and passenger flow.

Once completed, the overall capacity of the airport is expected to increase to around 15 million passengers annually, strengthening Sri Lanka’s position as a regional aviation hub, officials said.

title: Early rally fades as profit-taking leaves market mixed - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Almas Equities Research

The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) ended Tuesday’s session on a mixed note, with the All Share Price Index (ASPI) closing marginally lower while the S&P SL20 Index managed to post a slight gain. The market began the day on a strong footing, with the ASPI surging more than 180 points during the first half hour of trading as buying interest supported broad market momentum.

However, the early optimism proved difficult to sustain, as profit-taking gradually emerged across several counters throughout the session. The selling pressure erased most of the intraday gains, resulting in a largely flat close despite the strong start. The session highlighted the market’s continued struggle to establish a clear direction, with investors balancing short-term profit-taking against selective accumulation of fundamentally strong stocks.

Investor participation remained healthy, particularly among value investors, as crossing transactions accounted for more than 40% of total market turnover. This suggests continued confidence in selected counters despite the cautious broader market environment.

The Materials sector dominated trading activity, generating LKR 1.55 billion in turnover from 52.41 million shares traded. CIC.N emerged as the sector’s top contributor, recording LKR 1.42 billion in turnover with 44.45 million shares changing hands.

The ASPI declined by 3.36 points, or 0.02%, to close at 22,377.29, while the S&P SL20 Index edged up by 1.79 points, or 0.03%, to close at 6,221.32.

Total market turnover stood at LKR 3.85 billion, while share volume reached 152.55 million shares. Crossing transactions amounted to LKR 1.61 billion, representing 42% of total turnover. The largest crossing was recorded in CIC.N, generating LKR 1.18 billion in turnover with 36.95 million shares traded.

Market breadth remained broadly balanced, with 108 gainers and 106 decliners, reflecting mixed investor sentiment amid heightened intraday volatility.

Among the positive contributors, SUN.N led gains with a contribution of 4.19 points, followed by COMB.N, SPEN.N, ASCO.N, and LFIN.N. On the downside, CARG.N emerged as the largest drag on the index, shedding 6.59 points, while CINS.N, SAMP.N, NDB.N, and CFIN.N also weighed on market performance.

Among notable trades, SINS.N recorded significant activity with a turnover of LKR 0.14 billion and 1.89 million shares traded. The counter closed 3.86% lower, reflecting the profit-taking pressure observed across selected stocks during the session.

title: Only option left for Sallay is to reveal what he knows: Govt. - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Cabinet spokesman and Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said that the most appropriate step that former intelligence chief Suresh Sallay can take in relation to the Easter Sunday terror attacks is to disclose all information in his possession and assist the ongoing investigations.

Speaking at the weekly media briefing to announce Cabinet decisions today (16), the Minister said that there was no value in withholding information known to him as a former intelligence and military officer.

“Whatever it is, the best thing that Suresh Sallay can do as an intelligence and military officer is to reveal what he knows about the Easter Sunday attack and support the security agencies,” he said.

He also stressed that efforts should not be directed at changing investigators, but rather at cooperating with the Criminal Investigation Department and providing relevant data.

Commenting on Sallay’s detention, the Minister said he is being held under standard procedures used for detainees under detention orders, with no special cell or privileges provided.

He added that all necessary medical and humanitarian care is being ensured, while authorities continue to provide him with required nutrition and allow family members to visit and provide food. Medical attention has also been given without delay when required, he noted.

title: Dubai-based Indian expat dies after sudden on-field collapse during cricket match - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
THE TIMES OF INDIA - A 38-year-old Indian expatriate who had lived in Dubai for nearly 15 years, died after collapsing during a routine cricket match.

Mohammed Safwan Shanu hails from Bhatkal in Karnataka Safwan was batting during a weekly Sunday morning cricket game when he suddenly collapsed on the pitch at around 7.10am. Teammates rushed to help and called an ambulance. CPR was administered before he was taken to the hospital, where doctors later declared him dead on arrival.

Friends said there had been no indication that anything was wrong. The evening before the match, Safwan had visited Dubai's Waterfront Market with friends to buy fish and groceries before preparing for the game, a long-standing weekend routine.

A close friend of Safwan Nabeel Karikal, who was with him on the field, told Khaleej Times that everything appeared normal before the incident.

"We play cricket every Sunday morning, and this has become our routine for years. On Saturday evening, we went to the Waterfront Market to buy fish and groceries. He was perfectly fine. The next morning, we even travelled together in the same car to the ground, and everything was normal," Nabeel said.

He added, "Safwan suddenly collapsed and lost consciousness while batting. We immediately called for an ambulance. CPR was performed, and he was rushed to the hospital. We later came to know that doctors had declared him dead on arrival."

Safwan moved to the UAE around 15 years ago and built his life in Dubai, where he lived with his wife and their four children, three sons and a daughter born just four months ago.

After working for a private company for about eight years, he later started his own business. Outside work, he was widely known for his involvement in community cricket, having captained teams and won numerous player-of-the-match and tournament awards over the years.

Community leader Muniri Atiqur Rahman, who had known Safwan since childhood, said he would be remembered not only for his achievements on the cricket field but also for his character and relationships with others.

Safwan's parents wanted to travel from India to Dubai to attend the funeral, but did not have UAE visas. Relatives stepped in to coordinate the visa process, complete the necessary documentation and arrange travel so they could reach Dubai in time for their son's final rites.

Friends said cricket remained a constant throughout Safwan's life, from his childhood in Bhatkal to his years in Dubai, where he became a familiar figure in local cricket circles.

title: “Some may feel law is moving in their direction”, says Govt spokesperson - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Cabinet Spokesperson Nalinda Jayatissa has stated that any decision on arrest or non-arrest will be based strictly on evidence uncovered during ongoing investigations, in remarks linked to the legal developments involving former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa.

“Arrest or non-arrest will be decided based on what is revealed during the investigation. As the investigation proceeds correctly, one might feel it is moving in their direction,” Jayatissa said, responding to reports that Gotabaya Rajapaksa had sought a court order to prevent a possible arrest under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.

He added that investigations will continue under established legal procedures, with outcomes determined by the findings of the inquiry.

title: Health system could face severe strain if Dengue cases continue to rise: Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The healthcare system could come under severe pressure if the number of dengue patients continues to increase, Cabinet Spokesperson and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa warned today.

Speaking at the weekly Cabinet media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa said some hospitals, particularly in Colombo, are already experiencing overcrowding due to the growing number of dengue admissions.

“If patient numbers increase further, the hospital system may not be able to cope. We must reduce the number of infections,” he said.

The Minister stressed that preventing dengue transmission remains the most effective way to ease the burden on hospitals and healthcare workers. He urged the public to actively support ongoing dengue prevention programmes and eliminate mosquito breeding sites in their homes, schools, workplaces and surrounding environments.

Dr. Jayatissa noted that health authorities are closely monitoring the situation and have intensified dengue control activities in high-risk areas across the country.

He expressed confidence that the current rise in cases could be brought under control if the public fully cooperates with this week’s nationwide dengue prevention campaign.

title: Sri Lanka preparing contingency plans for potential El Niño impact - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Government is closely monitoring the anticipated El Niño climate phenomenon and is formulating plans to address its potential impacts, Cabinet Spokesman and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said today (16).

Speaking at the weekly Cabinet media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa said several rounds of discussions have already been held under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to assess the possible effects of the weather pattern and prepare appropriate responses.

He noted that ministers have also discussed measures that can be implemented at the ministerial level to mitigate any challenges that may arise.

The Minister further stated that the Government is paying close attention to forecasts issued by the Department of Meteorology and is developing contingency plans based on weather conditions that could emerge over the coming year.

title: UN Resident Coordinator meets NCW Chairperson in Colombo - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka, Marc-André Franche, met with the newly appointed Chairperson of the National Commission on Women (NCW), Grace Asirwatham, at the Commission’s office in Colombo.

At the outset of the meeting, the Resident Coordinator congratulated the Chairperson on her appointment and reaffirmed the United Nations’ continued commitment to supporting the National Commission on Women in fulfilling its mandate under the Women Empowerment Act No. 37 of 2024. He was accompanied by representatives of UN Women Sri Lanka, while Commissioners of the NCW also participated in the discussions.

Welcoming the UN delegation, the Chairperson expressed appreciation for the ongoing support provided by the United Nations system, particularly through UN Women, in strengthening the operational capacity of the Commission. She noted the importance of technical assistance in developing institutional procedures, systems, and stakeholder engagement frameworks.

The Chairperson further outlined the key objectives of the Women Empowerment Act and highlighted the role of the National Commission on Women as an independent statutory body mandated to promote and protect the rights of women in Sri Lanka. She also briefed the delegation on progress made in establishing the Commission, including the development of governance structures, coordination mechanisms, and institutional capacity-building initiatives.

The Resident Coordinator reaffirmed the United Nations’ continued support for the operationalisation of the Commission and agreed to facilitate further engagement with relevant UN technical teams to explore areas of cooperation in priority areas.

The meeting concluded with a shared commitment to strengthening collaboration between the United Nations and the National Commission on Women in advancing women’s rights, promoting gender equality, and supporting women’s empowerment across Sri Lanka.
